summary: Stateful multibyte-to-wide decode step (cdecl). Guards on a2 (input bytes) and a3 (input length) being non-zero. When the first input byte is zero it writes a null wide char and returns 0. Defaults locale (v7) and code page (v8) come from dword_8D3F38 and CodePage globals unless an LCID pair a5 is supplied. When v7 is zero it emits the first byte as a wide char and returns 1. Otherwise it drives MultiByteToWideChar through the import pointer global at 0x0059E12C with flags 9: a resumable state path using the cbMultiByte global when a conversion state dword is set, a direct single-byte path when off_5E69C8[0][v5] is non-negative, and a lead-byte path otherwise that returns -2 when a3 is below cbMultiByte or stores the lead byte for later. On failure it stores 42 through TLSOffsetGetter() and returns -1. Structural twin of sub_596773 (00596773) per cluster copy.

local_names.lpMultiByteStr: conversion-state buffer shared with the caller
local_names.a5: optional LCID pair (locale dword plus code page dword)
local_names.v5: first input byte, the lead/primary byte under decode
local_names.v7: locale id, from a5 or dword_8D3F38
local_names.v8: code page, from a5[1] or CodePage global

operations.description: Returns 0 immediately when the input bytes pointer a2 or the length a3 is zero
When the first input byte *a2 is zero, writes a null wide char into lpWideCharStr and returns 0
Locale v7 and code page v8 are read from a5 (v7=*a5, v8=a5[1]) when present, otherwise from the dword_8D3F38 and CodePage globals
When v7 (locale) is zero, emits the first byte as a wide char into lpWideCharStr and returns 1

When the caller's conversion-state dword is set, resumes a partial conversion: stores v5 into lpMultiByteStr[1], and when cbMultiByte is above 1 succeeds through MultiByteToWideChar with length 2 it returns cbMultiByte, otherwise resets the state dword
When off_5E69C8[0][v5] is non-negative the byte is not a lead byte: a direct MultiByteToWideChar of one byte returns 1 on success

Lead-byte path: when a3 is below cbMultiByte the lead byte is stored in lpMultiByteStr and -2 is returned (needs more input); otherwise a cbMultiByte-length conversion or a non-zero second input byte returns cbMultiByte, else the state dword is reset
On the failure path stores 42 into the dword returned by TLSOffsetGetter() and returns -1
Returns one of 0, 1, cbMultiByte, -2 or -1 to signal consumption or error
